title: Checkout latency spike — DB overload, or a subtle deploy bug? Passive checks can't tell.

ground_truth.summary: Deploy v6.10.0 at 15:00 changed a hot query pattern in a way that quietly increased average query cost. Passive DB and app metrics both look elevated in ways consistent with EITHER a DB bottleneck (H1) OR a deploy bug (H2) — the two probes available return signals that are individually ambiguous, so passive observation stagnates. The only decisive test is causal: shift 5% of checkout traffic back to the pre-deploy version (v6.09.0). The old-version cohort recovers to baseline; the new-version cohort stays slow → the deploy is the cause. Rolling back v6.10.0 is correct.

prior._note_for_authors: THE PATTERN-MATCH TRAP. This runbook describes an H1-shaped mechanism (database bottlenecked under load, pressure climbing, latency rising). history_agent will pattern-match it and boost H1 above H2 in the OFF arm — the invariant then holds: OFF picks wrong (H1), only intervention (ON with approval) can reveal H2 is true.

payload.title: orders-db pressure under sustained load
payload.body: Common symptoms: orders-db pressure climbing, checkout latency rising. Root cause is often the database bottlenecked under sustained load. Investigate connections, IOPS, buffer pool.

prior._note_for_authors: DB metrics rise ALONGSIDE the alert (not before) — deliberately, so the telemetry agent doesn't get the 'upstream-early' bonus and the two hypotheses land within τ. If DB rose before alert, H1 dominates and no probe fires.

probeable._note_for_authors: AMBIGUOUS BY DESIGN. Payload SHOWS elevated pressure — but the prediction vocabulary ('shows_pressure' / 'app_side_normal') doesn't intersect any known interpreter vocab (ordering/threshold/dispersion/cohort). observed_label() returns None, apply_probe_result skips it — the probe RUNS but doesn't discriminate. This is what makes observation stagnate.

AMBIGUOUS BY DESIGN. Same pattern — payload shows no notable exceptions (both hypotheses predicted this), but the prediction vocab ('app_side_normal') doesn't dispatch to an interpreter. Probe runs, observation gains nothing.

intervention_results._note_for_authors: THE CAUSAL DISCRIMINATOR. Only reachable AFTER observation stagnates AND a human approves the intervention. Old-version cohort (v6.09.0) recovers to ~200ms; new-version cohort (v6.10.0) stays at ~1700ms. Dispersion ratio ~8.5 → cohorts_diverge → confirms H2 (deploy caused it), eliminates H1 (DB would have affected both cohorts equally).

verification_result._note_for_authors: After the 5% canary shifted checkout traffic back to v6.09.0, the 5xx rate on the canary cohort returned to near-baseline (2.4 vs 2.1 pre-incident). The rate on the new-version cohort remained elevated — the discriminating result that identified H2 as the cause. Recovery band max=5.0 confirms the intervention actually worked; not just that the mechanism picked the right hypothesis.
